name: Lumbini
summary: In the plains of southern Nepal, Lumbini is where Queen Maya Devi gave birth to Siddhartha Gautama, who became the Buddha. The Maya Devi Temple shelters the marker stone of his birth, and a long monastic zone holds temples built by Buddhist nations around the world.
seasonNote: October to March is dry and mild; December and January can be foggy. April to June is very hot, and the monsoon (June to September) brings heavy rain. Buddha Jayanti in April or May is the main festival.
arrival: Fly from Kathmandu to Gautam Buddha International Airport at Bhairahawa (about 40 minutes), then 30 minutes by road. Buses run from Kathmandu and Pokhara (8 to 10 hours) and from the Indian border at Sunauli.
gettingAround: The sacred garden is car-free; rent a bicycle or rickshaw for the 4 km monastic zone.
cashTip: Carry Nepali rupees; ATMs are in Bhairahawa, and cards work only in bigger hotels.
foodTip: Dal bhat (rice with lentils and curries), momos, and simple vegetarian meals at monastery guesthouses.
buyTip: Prayer flags, singing bowls, Buddha statues and Nepali tea.
baseArea: Hotels and monastery guesthouses near the sacred garden

connections.note: To Bhairahawa, then 30 minutes by road.

items.name: Maya Devi Temple
items.summary: A simple white temple over ancient ruins and the marker stone showing the exact spot of the Buddha's birth.
items.expect: Shoes off; no photos inside; an entry fee for foreigners.
items.tip: Come at dawn when monks chant under the Bodhi tree beside the sacred pond.
items.why: One of the four holiest places in Buddhism and a World Heritage Site.
flow: Temple, then the pond and the Bodhi tree.

items.name: Ashoka Pillar
items.summary: A stone pillar raised by Emperor Ashoka in 249 BC, with an inscription naming this as the Buddha's birthplace.
items.expect: Beside the Maya Devi Temple.
items.tip: Read the translation on the sign beside it.
items.why: The 2,300-year-old proof that this is the place.

items.name: Monastic Zone
items.summary: A long canal-side park of monasteries built by China, Thailand, Myanmar, Germany, Vietnam, Korea and others.
items.expect: Spread over 4 km; many close at midday.
items.tip: Rent a bicycle and visit the Thai, Chinese and German monasteries.
items.why: Buddhist architecture from across the world in one place.

items.name: World Peace Pagoda
items.summary: A gleaming white stupa built by Japanese Buddhists, with a golden Buddha.
items.expect: At the far end of the monastic zone.
items.tip: Go at sunset when it glows.
items.why: A calm place to end a day of temples.

items.name: Lumbini Museum and Eternal Peace Flame
items.summary: The ever-burning peace flame by the central canal, and a museum of the region's Buddhist history.
items.expect: Small; check opening hours.
items.tip: Walk the canal to the flame on the way to the pagoda.

items.name: Tilaurakot (ancient Kapilavastu)
items.summary: The ruined palace city where the young prince Siddhartha is believed to have grown up.
items.expect: About an hour by car; ruins in forest.
items.tip: Hire a driver and combine with nearby Kudan and Gotihawa.

items.name: Dal bhat
items.summary: Nepal's everyday meal of rice, lentil soup, vegetable curry and pickles, refilled for free.
items.expect: Simple local restaurants.
items.tip: Ask for refills; they're usually included.

items.name: Momo stalls
items.summary: Steamed or fried dumplings with tomato and sesame chutney.
items.expect: Quick and cheap.
items.tip: Order a plate of steamed vegetable momos.

items.name: Monastery guesthouse meals
items.summary: Some monasteries offer simple vegetarian meals to visitors and guests.
items.expect: Fixed times; donations welcome.
items.tip: Ask at your guesthouse which kitchens are open.
items.why: A quiet meal in the spirit of the place.

name: Kandy
tagline: Sri Lanka's hill capital and the Temple of the Tooth
summary: The last royal capital of Sri Lanka, set around a lake in green hills. The Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic holds the Buddha's tooth and draws pilgrims from across the Buddhist world, especially for the Esala Perahera procession of drummers and decorated elephants.
seasonNote: January to April is driest. The Esala Perahera in July or August is the high point, with hotels booked months ahead. October and November bring the inter-monsoon rains.
arrival: Bandaranaike International Airport near Colombo is about 3 hours by road; the scenic train from Colombo takes about 3 hours.
gettingAround: Walk around the lake; tuk-tuks for everything else (use the PickMe app for fair fares).
cashTip: Carry rupees for tuk-tuks and temples; cards work in hotels.
foodTip: Rice and curry with many small dishes, hoppers (rice-flour pancakes) for breakfast, kottu roti at night and Ceylon tea.
buyTip: Ceylon tea, gemstones (buy only from licensed shops), batik and wooden masks.
baseArea: Around Kandy Lake or the hills above it

connections.note: Fly from Colombo airport, about 3 hours from Kandy.

items.name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
items.summary: The golden-roofed temple holding the Buddha's tooth relic, with drumming and offerings at the daily puja.
items.expect: Shoes off; shoulders and knees covered; an entry fee for foreigners.
items.tip: Go for the evening puja around 6:30pm, when the relic chamber opens.
items.why: Sri Lanka's most sacred Buddhist site.

items.name: Kandy Lake
items.summary: An 1807 lake built by the last king, with a shady walk around its cloud-wall edge.
items.expect: Busy at dusk; monkeys in the trees.
items.tip: Walk the full loop at sunset.

items.name: Royal Botanical Gardens, Peradeniya
items.summary: Huge gardens with an avenue of royal palms, an orchid house and giant fig trees.
items.expect: Bring water; bats hang in the trees.
items.tip: See the giant Javan fig tree and the orchid house.
items.why: One of Asia's finest botanical gardens.

items.name: Kandyan dance show
items.summary: An hour of drumming, acrobatic Kandyan dance and fire-walking.
items.expect: Nightly at 5pm.
items.tip: Go before the evening temple puja.

items.name: Bahirawakanda Buddha
items.summary: A giant white Buddha on a hilltop overlooking the city.
items.expect: Steep road; shoes off at the top.
items.tip: Go late afternoon for the view.

items.name: Udawatta Kele Sanctuary
items.summary: The old royal forest behind the temple, with trails, birds and monkeys.
items.expect: Quiet trails; leeches after rain.
items.tip: Walk early for birdwatching.
items.why: A rainforest in the middle of the city.
flow: Enter from the north of the lake.

items.name: Sigiriya
items.summary: A 5th-century palace on top of a 200 m rock, with frescoes and lion-paw gate.
items.expect: About 2.5 hours each way; 1,200 steps.
items.tip: Climb at opening to beat the heat; combine with Dambulla cave temples.

items.name: Rice and curry
items.summary: A plate of rice with many small curries, sambols and papadum.
items.expect: Best at lunch in local cafés.
items.tip: Try dhal, jackfruit curry and pol sambol.
items.why: The daily meal of Sri Lanka.

items.name: Hoppers
items.summary: Bowl-shaped rice-flour pancakes, often with an egg in the middle.
items.expect: Breakfast and evening.
items.tip: Order an egg hopper with lunu miris chilli relish.

items.name: Kottu roti
items.summary: Chopped roti stir-fried with vegetables, egg and curry on a hot plate, to a loud clatter.
items.expect: An evening dish.
items.tip: Listen for the clanging blades and follow the sound.
flow: Find a kottu shop at night.

name: Koyasan
tagline: A mountain of temples, and a night in a monastery
summary: The mountain-top home of Shingon Buddhism, founded by the monk Kūkai in 816, with over 100 temples. Stay overnight in a temple, eat monks' vegetarian food, join the dawn prayers, and walk through Okunoin, a vast forest cemetery of moss-covered graves lit by lanterns.
seasonNote: Cooler than the cities; autumn colour peaks in early November and spring is green. Winters are cold and snowy; the Mantō Kuyōe lantern festival is in mid-August.
arrival: From Osaka's Namba station take the Nankai line to Gokurakubashi, then the cable car up (about 2 hours in all).
gettingAround: Buses run along the main street; the temples are mostly walkable.
cashTip: Carry cash; some temples and small shops don't take cards.
foodTip: Shōjin ryōri, the vegetarian food of Buddhist monks, with sesame tofu and koya-dofu, served at temple lodgings.
buyTip: Prayer beads, incense, goshuin stamp books and koya-dofu.
baseArea: A shukubō temple lodging on the main street

items.name: Okunoin
items.summary: Japan's largest cemetery, with 200,000 graves under giant cedars on a 2 km path to Kūkai's mausoleum.
items.expect: No photos beyond the last bridge; very atmospheric at night.
items.tip: Join a monk-led night tour from Ichinohashi bridge.
items.why: One of the most magical walks in Japan.
flow: Walk to the Lantern Hall and mausoleum.

items.name: Kongōbu-ji
items.summary: The head temple of Shingon Buddhism, with painted sliding doors and Japan's largest rock garden.
items.expect: Tea and a sweet included.
items.tip: Sit by the Banryūtei rock garden.

items.name: Danjo Garan
items.summary: The temple complex with the bright vermilion Konpon Daitō pagoda, the centre of Kūkai's plan.
items.expect: Some halls charge a small fee.
items.tip: Go inside the Daitō to see the mandala of Buddhas.

items.name: Temple stay and dawn prayers
items.summary: A night in a temple lodging, with dinner, a futon on tatami and morning prayers with the monks.
items.expect: Book ahead; shared baths; early start.
items.tip: Choose a temple offering the fire ritual (goma) at dawn.

items.name: Daimon Gate
items.summary: The huge vermilion gate at the old entrance to the mountain, with guardian statues.
items.expect: A walk or bus from the centre.
items.tip: Come for sunset over the mountains.
items.why: The grand entrance to the sacred mountain.

items.name: Reihōkan Museum
items.summary: A museum of Buddhist art, with national treasures from Koyasan's temples.
items.expect: Rotating exhibits.
items.tip: Pair it with the Garan next door.

items.name: Shōjin ryōri
items.summary: Beautiful vegetarian Buddhist meals of many small dishes, served in temples.
items.expect: Included in temple stays; some temples serve lunch to visitors.
items.tip: Look for the sesame tofu (goma-dōfu).

items.name: Sesame tofu shops
items.summary: Shops making smooth goma-dōfu sesame tofu, a Koyasan speciality.
items.expect: Small portions; good for a snack.
items.tip: Try it with wasabi and soy.

items.name: Udon and soba cafés
items.summary: Simple noodle shops for lunch between temples.
items.expect: Close early.
items.tip: Eat lunch early; many close by 4pm.
items.why: Warming food on a cold mountain.

name: Ise
summary: Ise Grand Shrine is the holiest site of Shinto, dedicated to the sun goddess Amaterasu, and its wooden halls are rebuilt every 20 years. Walk the cedar forests of the Inner and Outer shrines, eat in the old pilgrim street of Oharai-machi, and see the wedded rocks on the coast nearby.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are pleasant. New Year brings millions for hatsumōde, the first shrine visit; summers are humid.
arrival: Kintetsu limited express trains from Osaka (about 1h 45m), Kyoto (about 2h) and Nagoya (about 1h 20m).
gettingAround: Buses link the Outer Shrine, Inner Shrine and the coast; tourist day passes are good value.
cashTip: Carry cash for offerings and food stalls.
foodTip: Thick Ise udon in dark sauce, Akafuku red-bean rice cakes, Ise lobster and Matsusaka beef.
buyTip: Akafuku sweets, Ise pearls from Toba, and shrine charms.

items.name: Ise Grand Shrine, Inner Shrine (Naikū)
items.summary: The inner shrine of the sun goddess Amaterasu, reached over the Uji Bridge through ancient cedar forest.
items.expect: Free; the main sanctuary is seen only through its gates; no photos at the inner hall.
items.tip: Visit the Outer Shrine first, as tradition says, and come early morning.
items.why: The most sacred site in Shinto.
flow: Purify at the Isuzu River, then walk to the main sanctuary.

items.name: Ise Grand Shrine, Outer Shrine (Gekū)
items.summary: The outer shrine of Toyouke, goddess of food, near Iseshi station.
items.expect: Free; quieter than the inner shrine.
items.tip: See the Sengūkan museum on the shrine's rebuilding.
items.why: Traditionally the first stop of an Ise pilgrimage.

items.name: Oharai-machi and Okage Yokochō
items.summary: The old pilgrim street outside the inner shrine, rebuilt in Edo style with food stalls and shops.
items.expect: Busy at midday.
items.tip: Snack your way down the street after the shrine.

items.name: Meoto Iwa (Wedded Rocks)
items.summary: Two sacred rocks in the sea joined by a heavy rope, at Futami Okitama Shrine.
items.expect: Short visit; sunrise between the rocks in early summer.
items.tip: Go at sunrise between May and July.
items.why: One of Japan's best-known sacred sights.

items.name: Mikimoto Pearl Island
items.summary: Where the first cultured pearl was made, with a museum and ama women divers.
items.expect: About 20 minutes by train.
items.tip: Watch the ama diving demonstration.
items.why: The birthplace of the cultured pearl.

items.name: Ago Bay
items.summary: A coast of islands and pearl rafts, with a viewpoint at Yokoyama.
items.expect: About 45 minutes by car or train.
items.tip: Go to the Yokoyama observatory at sunset.

items.name: Akafuku
items.summary: A 300-year-old shop serving soft rice cakes topped with sweet red bean paste and green tea.
items.expect: Queues, but fast.
items.tip: Sit inside by the kettle for tea and akafuku.

items.name: Ise udon
items.summary: Very soft, thick udon in a dark, sweet soy sauce, a pilgrim food for centuries.
items.expect: Cheap and quick.
items.tip: Order it with a raw egg on top.

items.name: Ise lobster and seafood
items.summary: Ise-ebi spiny lobster, oysters and abalone on the Shima coast.
items.expect: Expensive in season (October to April).
items.tip: Try grilled seafood cooked by ama divers in a diver's hut.
flow: Book a seafood lunch in Toba.

name: Ajmer · Pushkar
tagline: The Sufi shrine of Ajmer and the holy lake of Pushkar
summary: Ajmer is home to the dargah of the Sufi saint Moinuddin Chishti, India's most visited Muslim shrine, where people of every faith come with roses and chadars and qawwali music fills the courtyards. Over the hill, Pushkar's holy lake and rare Brahma temple make it one of Hinduism's sacred towns.
seasonNote: October to March is best. The Urs festival, marking the saint's death anniversary, moves with the Islamic calendar and draws huge crowds; the Pushkar Camel Fair is in October or November.
arrival: Ajmer Junction has fast trains from Jaipur (about 2 hours) and Delhi (about 6.5 hours). Kishangarh airport is 30 minutes away.
gettingAround: Rickshaws in Ajmer; buses and taxis to Pushkar (about 30 minutes). Pushkar is walkable.
cashTip: Carry cash for offerings, rickshaws and stalls; UPI is common.
foodTip: Biryani and kebabs near the dargah, sohan halwa sweets, and vegetarian rooftop cafés in Pushkar (Pushkar is meat- and alcohol-free).
buyTip: Rose petals and chadars at the dargah, silver jewellery and textiles in Pushkar.
baseArea: Pushkar guesthouses for calm; Ajmer near the station for convenience

items.name: Ajmer Sharif Dargah
items.summary: The shrine of the Sufi saint Moinuddin Chishti, with huge cooking cauldrons, marble courtyards and qawwali singers.
items.expect: Open to all faiths; cover your head; leave shoes at the stalls; very crowded on Thursdays and during Urs.
items.tip: Come on Thursday evening for qawwali in the courtyard.
items.why: One of the great Sufi shrines of the world.
flow: Offer roses at the tomb, then listen to qawwali.

items.name: Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra
items.summary: A 12th-century mosque built from temple stones, with carved pillars and arches.
items.expect: A short walk uphill from the dargah.
items.tip: Visit right after the dargah.
items.why: One of the oldest mosques in India.

items.name: Ana Sagar Lake
items.summary: A 12th-century lake with marble pavilions built by Shah Jahan on its banks.
items.expect: Boat rides; busy at sunset.
items.tip: Walk the Daulat Bagh gardens at sunset.

items.name: Soniji Ki Nasiyan
items.summary: A Jain temple with a hall of gilded models of the Jain universe.
items.expect: Only the golden hall is open to visitors.
items.tip: Look for the gilded flying ships in the hall.

items.name: Taragarh Fort
items.summary: A ruined hill fort with views over the city and lake.
items.expect: Steep road; jeeps run up.
items.tip: Go late afternoon for the view.

items.name: Pushkar Lake and Brahma Temple
items.summary: A holy lake ringed by 52 ghats and the Brahma Temple, one of very few in the world, over the hill from Ajmer.
items.expect: Shoes off on the ghats; politely refuse 'priests' offering paid blessings.
items.tip: Watch the evening aarti at Varaha Ghat and stay for sunset.
flow: Bus or taxi over the pass.

items.name: Dargah bazaar biryani
items.summary: Huge pots of biryani, kebabs and sweet zarda rice in the lanes around the shrine.
items.expect: Busy and simple.
items.tip: Try the biryani and seekh kebabs.

items.name: Sohan halwa shops
items.summary: Dense, ghee-rich sohan halwa with nuts, Ajmer's famous sweet.
items.expect: Sold by weight.
items.tip: Buy a small box to share.

items.name: Pushkar rooftop cafés
items.summary: Vegetarian rooftop cafés over the lake, from thalis to falafel.
items.expect: No meat, eggs or alcohol in Pushkar.
items.tip: Pick one facing the lake at sunset.
